notes: Advice for the orchestrator, not rules: it chooses freely among the models swarm{action:"models", all:true} lists. Cards summarize published evidence (sources and dates in docs/MODELS.md); the run's own outcomes (cogentic_models.outcomes_by_model) outweigh them. Update the cards when Google ships new models; a listed model without a card is simply new.
levels: Each family is served at thinking levels (low, medium, high, sometimes xhigh). Higher levels think longer: better on hard reasoning, slower, more tokens and quota. Pick the lowest level that the role's difficulty needs, and escalate on evidence.

carbon.positioning: Google's model for the hardest problems and long-horizon agentic work; uses many thinking tokens to explore hypotheses; listed for formal proofs and extended verification loops.
strengths: deepest single-shot reasoning in the family (AA HLE-Diamond 69.1, CritPt 69.0, RiemannBench 80.0)
weaknesses: slowest: ~56 tok/s, ~73 s to first answer token, ~37 min per AA index task at high
carbon.notes: Medium is close to high on AA (58.3 vs 60.0) at lower cost; Google describes Carbon as based on Argon.

neon.positioning: Complex coding, analytical reasoning and long-running agent workflows; deeper than Hydrogen and faster than Carbon.
strengths: top AA Intelligence Index (59.6 high, 61.4 xhigh)
weaknesses: lowest non-hallucination of the family (86.1%): check its citations
verbose, especially xhigh (283M output tokens on the AA suite)

hydrogen.positioning: Fast, cost-efficient execution for everyday and agentic work, on its own or as sub-agents; not Google's pick for the hardest reasoning.
strengths: fastest (~165 tok/s, ~8.6 min per AA task at high, 1.5 min at low)
weaknesses: clearly behind Carbon and Neon on the hardest reasoning
higher unjustified-refusal rate on multimodal prompts

roles.orchestrator: Long-running, tool-heavy coordination; no mathematics. Needs reliability more than depth. The conversation's own model; suggest a change to the user only if it is clearly unsuited.
roles.literature: Web search and reading; exact citations matter most (low hallucination), plus speed for many fetches. Depth only for a targeted mid-run search on a hard technical step.
roles.summarizer: Read a long history, select and condense; one per prover slot, so it is called often. Needs long-context reading and economy more than depth.
roles.prover: The hardest work: research-level proofs. Needs maximum reasoning depth. Diversify models within a round so provers do not share blind spots; give repair/finalize slots a strong model too.
roles.solo_verifier: Adversarial line-by-line check of one draft. Needs depth and strictness and low hallucination; prefer a different model from the draft's prover.
roles.cross_verifier: Reads all drafts of a round side by side: long context plus depth; prefer a model different from most of the round's provers.
roles.auditor: Faithful restatement of confirmed fragments as self-contained lemmas: precision and low hallucination, moderate depth.
roles.lemma_verifier: Adversarial check of one short lemma: depth over speed, but short inputs, so a medium level is usually enough.
roles.advisor: Process analysis of logs across the run; no mathematics. Long reading, short output: economy.
roles.comparator: Judge which verified proof is strongest: moderate depth.
roles.writer: Long, faithful exposition of a verified proof: long output (prefer 64K-output models), clarity, no new mathematics.
roles.final_auditor: Last gate against errors introduced in exposition: maximum strictness.
roles.narrator: Maintains the swarm Overview: the cheapest, fastest model.
roles.monitor: Watches for stalls: the cheapest, fastest model.

selection_principles: Prefer the newest, strongest generation the list offers (today Gemini 4: Carbon, Neon, Hydrogen; later Gemini 5 and beyond). Models older than Gemini 4 are weaker: avoid them. Gemini 4 Argon is being retired: avoid it.
Spend depth where errors are expensive (provers, verifiers, final audit) and economy where they are cheap (summaries, narration, process advice).
priority=quality: prefer the deepest suitable model and higher levels; priority=economy: prefer faster, cheaper models and lower levels, escalating only on evidence; balanced: in between.
Diversify: different provers in a round on different models; a verifier on a different model from the prover it checks.

Adapt on evidence from cogentic_models: a model whose drafts keep failing on depth gets replaced or escalated a level; a verifier model that missed errors another caught gets replaced for that role; a role that keeps succeeding on a cheaper model stays there.

Watch the budget and quota: as remaining calls shrink, move low-stakes roles to cheaper levels before cutting prover slots; if a worker pauses on quota, switch it with swarm{action:"model"} to another suitable model.

A listed model without a card is new: read what you can about it (its name, its level, a quick look at Google's model card if you have web access), try it on low-stakes roles first, compare outcomes, then promote it.
User pins and single_model always win.
